cards.text: Last time, David took Uriah's wife and had Uriah killed, and what he did was evil in the sight of the LORD. Now the LORD sends Nathan the prophet to David. Nathan doesn't walk in with a speech, friend. He walks in with a story.

cards.question: Nathan's story starts with two men in a certain city. How are they different?

answers.text: One is rich and one is poor
One is old and one is young
One is a king and one is a servant

cards.question: In Nathan's story, the rich man has a great number of sheep and cattle.

cards.text: The poor man has just one small ewe lamb he bought, and it shares his food, drinks from his cup and sleeps in his ARMS. Friend, that lamb has it better than most house cats.

cards.question: The poor man's lamb grew up with him and his children. Nathan says it was like what to him?

cards.text: Then a traveler comes to the rich man, who needs to prepare something for his guest. Remember, this guy has a GREAT number of sheep and cattle, enough to host the whole city and still have a herd left over.

cards.question: With all those animals of his own, what does the rich man prepare for the traveler?

answers.text: A calf from his own herd

cards.text: Nathan's story lands HARD. David burns with anger against the man who did this, and friend, the king is HOT.

cards.question: David swears by the life of the LORD. What does he say the man who did this deserves?
David also says the man must pay for the lamb. How many times over?

cards.text: So the king has handed down the sentence. Then Nathan looks right at David.

cards.question: What does Nathan tell King David?

cards.text: Oh, friend. David just sentenced the rich man. And the rich man is him.
Then Nathan brings a message from the LORD. God reminds David that He anointed him king, rescued him from Saul, the king before him, and gave him Israel and Judah.

cards.question: The LORD tells David that if all that wasn't enough, He would have given him even more.

cards.text: Then comes the hard question: why did David despise the LORD's command by doing evil in His sight? He put Uriah the Hittite to the sword and took his wife as his own.

cards.question: The LORD says David killed Uriah with the sword of which people?
Because David despised the LORD and took Uriah's wife, what does the LORD say will never depart from David's house?

cards.text: And the LORD says He will raise up adversity against David from his own house. Before David's very eyes, his wives will be given to another.

cards.question: David acted in secret. How does the LORD say He will do this thing?

answers.text: In broad daylight before all Israel

cards.text: The message is done, and every word of it just landed on the king. Now it's David's turn to speak.

cards.question: What does David say to Nathan?

answers.text: I have sinned against the LORD
I will pay it back four times

cards.question: Nathan replies to David. What does he say the LORD has done?
David said the man in the story deserves to die. Nathan tells David that he will not die.

cards.text: But then Nathan says, "Nevertheless." Because by this deed David showed utter contempt for the word of the LORD, the son born to him will surely die.
Nathan goes home. Then the LORD strikes the child that Uriah's wife bore to David, and the boy becomes ill.

cards.question: David's son is sick. What does David do?

answers.text: He pleads with God and fasts
He sends for Nathan to come back
He goes out to join the battle

cards.text: David spends the night lying in sackcloth on the ground. The elders of his household stand beside him to help him up.

cards.question: When the elders of his household come to help, David gets up and eats with them.

cards.text: On the seventh day, the child dies. And David's servants are afraid to tell him.

cards.question: The servants say David wouldn't listen to them while the child was alive. What are they afraid he might do now?

cards.text: But David sees his servants whispering to one another, and he picks up on it.

cards.question: David asks his whispering servants a question. What is it?

cards.text: "He is dead," they reply. Then David gets up from the ground.

cards.question: What does David do after he gets up from the ground?

answers.text: He washes and goes to worship
He tears his clothes and weeps

cards.question: After he worships in the house of the LORD, David goes home and asks for food.

cards.text: His servants can't make sense of it. They ask, "What is this you have done?" He fasted and wept while the child was alive, and now he gets up and eats.

cards.question: David answers his servants. Why did he fast and weep while the child was still alive?

answers.text: He hoped the LORD might let him live
Nathan had told him to do it
It was the custom for a king

cards.question: Now that the child is dead, why does David say he won't fast anymore?

answers.text: He can't bring the child back
The LORD spoke to him again

cards.text: Then David comforts his wife Bathsheba, and she gives birth to another son.

cards.question: What do David and Bathsheba name their new son?
The LORD sends word through Nathan the prophet to give the baby another name: Jedidiah. Why?

findings.problem: The card states facts from the previous chapter (David took Uriah's wife, had Uriah killed, and it was evil in the sight of the LORD, 2 Samuel 11) but cites only 2 Samuel 12:1. Those outside facts carry no reference, and the citation doesn't cover the verses the card uses.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences. That is over the limit.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences.

findings.problem: "A sheepdog" isn't the same kind of answer as "A daughter" and "A servant", which are both people. It also reads as a joke option next to the tender right answer.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card restates that the rich man has a great number of sheep and cattle, which comes from 2 Samuel 12:2. It cites only 2 Samuel 12:4. The citation should be 2 Samuel 12:2-4.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "So the king has handed down the sentence" recaps 2 Samuel 12:5-6, which was just asked on cards 2 and 3. The card cites only 12:7.
This story card tells no new part of the passage. It only reacts to "You are that man" from card 5, so it doesn't move the baker forward. The punchline could ride along on card 7 instead.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has 3 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card leaves out that the LORD gave David his master's house and his master's wives (2 Samuel 12:8). That detail mirrors the rich man's many flocks in the parable, and it sets up the wives in 12:11. No card tells it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has 3 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: David's closing words in 2 Samuel 12:23, "I will go to him, but he will not return to me", are never told on any card. Card 14 asks only about "Can I bring him back again?" This is a key line of David's answer.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
